source_refs.note: Exercise 14.3, Question 14: moment about B(3, -2, 3) of F = 6i + 4j - 4k acting at A, r = BA (book p.283). Answer key PDF 312: -14j - 14k.

blocks.prompt: 14. A force \(\underline{F} = 6\underline{i} + 4\underline{j} - 4\underline{k}\) is applied at the point \(A(1, -1, 2)\). Find the moment of the force about the point \(B(3, -2, 3)\).
blocks.explanation:
A moment-of-force question.
We must find the moment (a vector) of \(\underline{F}\) about \(B\).
Plan: \(\underline{r} = \underline{BA}\), then \(\underline{r} \times \underline{F}\) by the determinant.
steps:
Given: force \(\underline{F}\) acting through \(A(1, -1, 2)\); point \(B(3, -2, 3)\).
To find: the moment of \(\underline{F}\) about \(B\).
Method: Moment \(= \underline{r} \times \underline{F}\) (14.3.7 (c)), where \(\underline{r}\) is the vector from the point \(B\) (about which we turn) to a point \(A\) on the line of action of the force. The force is given in components.

Write the force
\[\underline{F} = 6\underline{i} + 4\underline{j} - 4\underline{k}\]
Why: Its components are the rows we need in the determinant.

Find \(\underline{r} = \underline{BA}\)
\[\underline{BA} = (1 - 3)\underline{i} + (-1 - (-2))\underline{j} + (2 - 3)\underline{k}\]
\[= -2\underline{i} + \underline{j} - \underline{k}\]
Why: \(\underline{r}\) starts at the point \(B\) about which the moment is taken and ends at the point \(A\) where the force acts.

Write the determinant
\[\underline{r} \times \underline{F} = \begin{vmatrix} \underline{i} & \underline{j} & \underline{k} \\ -2 & 1 & -1 \\ 6 & 4 & -4 \end{vmatrix}\]
Why: Row 1 holds the unit vectors, row 2 the components of the first vector \(\underline{r}\), row 3 those of the second \(\underline{F}\). The order of the rows follows the order of the product.

Work out the three minors
\[\underline{i}\text{ minor} = (1)(-4) - (-1)(4) = 0\]
\[\underline{j}\text{ minor} = (-2)(-4) - (-1)(6) = 14\]
\[\underline{k}\text{ minor} = (-2)(4) - (1)(6) = -14\]
Why: For each unit vector cover its row and column; the minor is (top-left)(bottom-right) minus (top-right)(bottom-left).

Attach the signs \(+, -, +\)
\[\underline{r} \times \underline{F} = \underline{i}(0) - \underline{j}(14) + \underline{k}(-14)\]
\[= -14\underline{j} - 14\underline{k}\]
Why: Expanding a determinant along row 1 uses the sign pattern \(+, -, +\); the middle (\(\underline{j}\)) term is subtracted.

Magnitude of the moment
\[|\underline{r} \times \underline{F}| = \sqrt{(0)^2 + (-14)^2 + (-14)^2}\]
\[= \sqrt{392} = 14 \sqrt{2}\]
Why: The length tells how strong the turning effect is.

Check
\[(\underline{r} \times \underline{F}) \cdot \underline{F} = (0)(6) + (-14)(4) + (-14)(-4)\]
\[= 0 - 56 + 56 = 0\]
Why: The moment \(\underline{r} \times \underline{F}\) must be perpendicular to \(\underline{F}\) (and to \(\underline{r}\)); the dot product is 0.
